description:
FILED s521c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18) from the #1576 one-file acceptance run of Path-Tiny t/locking.t (both subtests: "subprocess failed to get lock" got 2 expected 0; "subprocess managed to get lock" got 2 expected 1).

`system LIST` does not run the '""' overload of an OBJECT argument: it passes the referent's plain stringification.

REPRO (probed, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on 68aeebf5 + s521c, scratch/s521c/pr/sysx.pl):
    use Path::Tiny; my $t = Path::Tiny->tempfile; $t->spew("exit 3;\n");
    print system($^X, $t) >> 8, "\n";       # perl 3;  PCL 2 + stderr: Can't open perl script "ARRAY(0x2)"
    print system($^X, "$t") >> 8, "\n";     # 3 in both
Layer: the runtime's system / exec argument stringification (the overload-aware to-string, as print/join use).  Check exec, the pipe opens' LIST form and `qx` interpolation for the same miss.
REACH: Path-Tiny locking.t rows 1-2; any `system($^X, $path_obj)`.
subject: system LIST does not run the '""' overload of an object argument (passes ARRAY(0x2)) -- Path-Tiny locking.t: system($^X, $path_tiny_obj) runs a script named 'ARRAY(0x2)'
